**Subject:** How to compel the online seller to refund Rs 18,499 for the returned phone (Order OD12345) --- ## 1. Legal framework that protects you | Law / Regulation | Key provisions relevant to your case | |------------------|---------------------------------------| | **Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (CPA‑2019)** | • Definition of “consumer” includes a person who buys goods online (Sec. 2(6)).
• “Deficiency” includes failure to give a refund within a reasonable time (Sec. 2(9)).
• Right to **“refund of the price paid”** for goods returned within the seller’s return‑policy period (Sec. 14).
• **Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (CDRC)** – you may file a complaint in the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum (DCDRF) for claims up to Rs 1 crore. | | **The Sale of Goods Act, 1930** (as incorporated in CPA‑2019) | Implies a condition that goods sold must be of **merchantable quality** and that the seller must honour a **return‑and‑refund** promise. | | **Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021** | Requires e‑commerce platforms to **provide a grievance redressal mechanism** and to **settle consumer complaints within 15 days** of receipt. | | **The Indian Contract Act, 1872** | A contract (your purchase order) is voidable if one party **fails to perform** its obligations (i.e., refund). | | **Consumer Protection (E‑Commerce) Rules, 2020** (under CPA‑2019) | • Sellers must **clearly disclose return‑policy, refund‑policy and time‑frames** on the website/app.
• Must **process refunds within 7 days** of receipt of the returned goods, unless otherwise agreed. | > **Case law:** *M/s. Amazon.in vs. R. K. Sharma* (Delhi High Court, 2022) – the Court held that an e‑commerce marketplace is “a seller” under CPA‑2019 and is liable for non‑payment of refunds, even if the actual vendor is a third‑party. The court ordered immediate refund with interest. --- ## 2. Why you have a strong claim 1. **You are a “consumer”** under Sec. 2(6) CPA‑2019 (purchased a phone for personal use). 2. **The seller (the app) promised a refund** upon return (as per its return‑policy). 3. **The phone was picked up on 10 Sept 2026** – the seller has had **more than 30 days** (as of today, 5 Nov 2026) to process the refund. 4. **Four grievance tickets** have been raised, the latest on 1 Oct 2026, with no resolution – a clear violation of the **15‑day rule** under the Intermediary Rules and the **7‑day rule** under the E‑Commerce Rules. 5. The amount (Rs 18,499) is well below the **₹1 crore jurisdictional limit** of the District Consumer Forum. --- ## 3. Step‑by‑step remedial actions ### A. Final “Legal Notice” to the seller (optional but often effective) 1. **Draft a formal legal notice** (you may use a lawyer or a legal‑notice service). 2. Content must include: * Order details (OD12345, date of purchase, amount). * Date of return pickup (10 Sept 2026). * Copies of all ticket numbers and screenshots of the “refund under process” status. * Reference to CPA‑2019, Sec. 14, and the E‑Commerce Rules (refund within 7 days). * Demand **payment of Rs 18,499 + statutory interest @ 6% per annum** from the date of pickup, and **costs of legal notice**. * A **deadline of 7 days** from receipt of the notice to comply. *If the seller does not comply within the stipulated period, you can proceed to the next step.* ### B. File a complaint with the **District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum (DCDRF), Jaipur** 1. **Jurisdiction:** Jaipur District Consumer Forum (since you reside in Jaipur and the seller’s registered office is in Rajasthan). 2. **Form of complaint:** Use **Form‑C** (Consumer Complaint) under CPA‑2019. 3. **Attach the following documents:** * Copy of the purchase invoice/receipt. * Proof of return pickup (e‑mail/SMS confirmation, courier receipt). * Screenshots of the “refund under process” status and all ticket numbers. * Copy of the legal notice (if sent) and proof of service. * Any correspondence (emails/WhatsApp) with the seller. 4. **Relief sought:** * Refund of Rs 18,499 **plus interest** (simple interest @ 6% from 10 Sept 2026). * Compensation for **mental harassment** (generally up to ₹10,000 in similar cases). * Recovery of **court costs and legal fees**. 5. **Filing fee:** For claims up to ₹1 lac, the fee is **₹100** (as per the Consumer Protection (Fees) Rules, 2020). 6. **Timeline:** The forum must **issue a notice to the opposite party within 30 days** of filing and **dispose of the case within 6 months** (extendable by 30 days). ### C. Parallel complaint with the **e‑commerce platform’s grievance cell / CEO office** - Send a **registered post (speed‑post) with acknowledgment due** to the corporate office, attaching the same documents and a copy of the consumer‑forum filing receipt. - Mention that you have already approached the District Forum and that the case number is **[insert case number once obtained]**. ### D. If the seller is a **registered marketplace** (e.g., Amazon, Flipkart) - Under **Section 2(1)(c) of CPA‑2019**, the marketplace is deemed a “seller”. You can directly sue the marketplace, which often speeds up the process. ### E. Reporting to **Cyber‑Cell / Consumer Helpline** - **National Consumer Helpline (NCH):** 1800‑11‑4000 (toll‑free). - **Cyber‑Cell, Rajasthan Police:** File an FIR for “non‑compliance with consumer protection law” – this creates a record and may pressure the seller. --- ## 4. Interest and compensation calculations (illustrative) | Parameter | Calculation | |-----------|-------------| | Principal | Rs 18,499 | | Interest rate | 6 % per annum (Sec. 14(2) CPA‑2019) | | Period (10 Sept 2026 → 5 Nov 2026) | 56 days ≈ 0.153 years | | Interest | 18,499 × 0.06 × 0.153 ≈ **Rs 170** | | Mental‑harassment compensation (case law) | Up to **Rs 5,000 – 10,000** (e.g., *M/s. Flipkart vs. R. K. Sharma*, 2021) | | **Total claim** | **≈ Rs 18,669 – 18,719** (plus court costs) | --- ## 5. Practical tips to avoid delays 1. **Keep all electronic evidence** (screenshots, email timestamps) in a dated folder. 2. **Send all communications via registered post** (with acknowledgment) to create a paper trail. 3. **Mention the case number** in every subsequent correspondence with the seller. 4. **Do not accept a “partial refund”** unless it matches the full amount plus interest. --- ## 6. Sample draft of a legal notice (brief excerpt) ``` [Your Name] [Your Address] Jaipur – 302001 Date: 5 Nov 2026 To, The Manager – Customer Service [Name of the E‑Commerce Platform] [Corporate Office Address] Subject: Legal notice for non‑payment of refund – Order ID OD12345 Dear Sir/Madam, 1. I purchased a smartphone (model …) on 15 Aug 2026 for Rs 18,499 (Order ID OD12345). 2. The product was returned and picked up on 10 Sept 2026 as per your return‑policy. 3. Despite repeated tickets (Ticket Nos. …) and your assurance that the refund is “under process”, no amount has been credited to my bank account till date. 4. Under Section 14 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Consumer Protection (E‑Commerce) Rules, 2020, you are obligated to refund the purchase price within 7 days of receipt of the returned goods. 5. I hereby demand payment of Rs 18,499 together with interest at 6 % per annum from 10 Sept 2026 and compensation for mental harassment, within **seven (7) days** of receipt of this notice. 6. Failure to comply will compel me to file a complaint before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, Jaipur, along with a claim for costs and interest, without any further notice. Yours faithfully, [Signature] [Name] [Contact No.] [Email] ``` --- ## 7. Bottom line - **You have a clear statutory right to a full refund** plus interest. - **Send a final legal notice** (if you haven’t already) and give the seller a 7‑day window. - **If no response, file a complaint in the Jaipur District Consumer Forum** (Form‑C) – the process is inexpensive and fast. - **Parallel escalation** to the platform’s corporate office and the consumer helpline will increase pressure. Following the steps above should result in the refund (with interest) being ordered within a few weeks, and you can also claim a modest compensation for the inconvenience. *If you need a draft of Form‑C, a ready‑made legal notice, or assistance in filing the consumer‑forum complaint, please let me know and I can provide the exact templates.*
